assumptions: The branch is made after the terms were compared with the snapshot and before the worktree is moved; the lead kept this order and design 6.5 says it. The remove still runs only after the branch, the kept refs and the snapshot.

Lead decision, fix round 2: a commit counts as held only when a branch reaches it, in the worktree's repository and, for an agent's worktree, in the main repository too. A tag, a remote-tracking ref, a kept ref and a stash do not count.

The kept branch of an agent's detached worktree is in the main repository. A branch of the agent repository that holds the commit still means no branch is made, because rule 5 keeps that repository while its branch is not landed.

A kept name is taken when its branch item is due, deferred or removing. When that item's branch is at the worktree's own commit, the Discard runs under the next name and writes no ref, because that branch holds the commit: this rests on the lead's statement that Veldo never deletes a branch.
In AC3, kept is read as: the agent repository and its item are left as they were (deferred by rule 5 in the row), and its branch holds every commit.

The crash rows make the process stop by an exception raised inside keep_branch, and write reconcile's deferral through the Reconciler's own defer; the whole reconcile run is not driven by the ticket suite. 156_veldo_0315_reconcile was run in fix round 3, once, under the gate lock: green after its two rows left stale by VELDO-0318 were changed.
The footprint was widened to control_space_reconcile.py and its synced copy on the lead's instruction that reconcile records the left branch.
Fixture process table and Docker reads do not establish host-reader readiness.
VELDO-0301 ac4/no-clock, VELDO-0307 ownership/removes-nothing and 14 rows of VELDO-0331 are red on the base too: inherited and left.
